# [G1 — Warming](../hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming")

*Generated by `scripts/pages/hypodraft_g1.py`: what the data held here can and cannot show about the hypothesis. Each marked statement links to what it rests on.*

**Draft, not a result.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-STATUS">The test this page specifies has not been run: no script in this repository computes the solubility term, the deficit or their slopes on the station panel, so no slope, share or null is reported here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-STATUS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The hypothesis, and why it needs splitting before it can be tested

[G1](../hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming") predicts “monotone worsening independent of load”, and offers that as why load reduction has not produced the expected recovery. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-ROUTES">Warming reaches near-bed oxygen by the routes it names — **solubility**, **stratification** and the **rate of respiration** — and only the first lowers near-bed oxygen whatever is consumed there; the other two act through the consumption beneath the stratified layer, which the load feeds.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-ROUTES "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-QUESTION">So [G1](../hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming")'s testable content is not *does oxygen fall* but **what share of the long-term fall is the solubility ceiling falling**.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-QUESTION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The observable consequence, stated so it can be falsified

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-CSAT">Per station-month, `C_sat` is the oxygen solubility at the panel's near-bed temperature and salinity, from a published solubility equation for seawater, in mg/l; then `O_bed = C_sat(T_bed, S_bed) − D`, so `dO/dt ≡ dC_sat/dt − dD/dt`.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-CSAT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-DEFICIT">`C_sat` is computed from temperature and salinity by an equation from outside the archive, so the first term is **computed, not estimated** from it. The deficit `D` is solubility-neutral by construction and carries the rest: consumption, failed ventilation, advection.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-DEFICIT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-A">**`G1-a`:** *the decline is not mostly solubility* — `dC_sat/dt` is a minority of `dO/dt`. Falsified if the solubility term equals or exceeds the observed decline.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-A "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-B">**`G1-b`:** *`dD/dt > 0`* — the deficit widens, as it must if warming drives respiration or stratification faster than ventilation recovers. Falsified by `dD/dt ≤ 0`, or by a `dD/dt` indistinguishable from the year-block null. `G1-b` carries the load-independence claim; `G1-a` decides whom the finding is about.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-B "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The data held, counted here

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-DATA">`docs/data/areas/stations_series.{json,bin}` holds [679,422](../SOURCES.md#F-b61d7944ec) station-months at [1,415](../SOURCES.md#F-fff0060a3d) stations, in [564](../SOURCES.md#F-008df4b99b) monthly slots from January 1980, each value a median per station and month. The variables the identity needs are held on: `oxy_bed` [76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-a95c664ddf), `temp_bed` [84,656](../SOURCES.md#F-2cd2cd8a94), `sal_bed` [83,309](../SOURCES.md#F-92d0ea9ce4), `temp_surf` [84,668](../SOURCES.md#F-a7381242a1) and `sal_surf` [83,341](../SOURCES.md#F-c18aa3ed5b) station-months.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-DATA "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-JOIN">No script here joins them or applies a plausibility filter; a station-month carrying every one of them can be no more common than the rarest, so the joined panel holds at most [76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-a95c664ddf) station-months before any filter.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-JOIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-BEDDEF">“Near the bed” and “near the surface” are not fixed depths: `stations_series.py` takes, for each cast, the values in the deepest and in the shallowest part of the cast's own sampled depth range, cut at the fraction `0.25` of that range, and puts every such value in a station-month into one median. So `D` can pair temperature, salinity and oxygen from different casts and depths.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-BEDDEF "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-PANELRULE">Trend panel = cells (station × calendar month) with at least [8](../SOURCES.md#F-70bbed3282) distinct years **and** a span of at least [15](../SOURCES.md#F-cf4daa7d28) years. Balanced variant = cells present in both 1990–1999 and 2015–2026. No script here builds either, so neither's size is known.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-PANELRULE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What the values carry

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-VALUES">*Values.* The panel holds values no water has: station-months of negative oxygen, which the flag record reads as sign inversions. A plausibility filter must be stated, and what each of its bounds removes counted, before any slope.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-VALUES "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-DECIMALS">*Precision.* Temperature in the CTD extract is mostly written with more than one decimal: of its [7,501,421](../SOURCES.md#F-a33f8c08bd) temperature rows, [1,076,874](../SOURCES.md#F-5bb29588ed) ([14.4](../SOURCES.md#F-b87ceb99d3)%) carry at most one decimal in the original result.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-DECIMALS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-CLOCK">*Hour.* The CTD extract the panel is built from has no time of day in any row and no column for it. If the sampling hour drifted over the record, the diel oxygen cycle drifted with it, and nothing inside the panel can correct it: this caps the test rather than bounds it. The water-chemistry extract does carry clock values, which can bound the hour only where a cast shares its day with a bottle.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-CLOCK "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-UNIT">*Unit.* The unit is a station: the panel deliberately carries no water body, and every estimate is within a cell of one station and one calendar month, so none is needed.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-UNIT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Circularity, avoided

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-SAT">Archived near-bed oxygen saturation (`oxysat_bed`) is held on [64,493](../SOURCES.md#F-1f76a99b02) station-months, fewer than the [76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-a95c664ddf) with near-bed oxygen.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-SAT "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-CIRC">It is computed from oxygen, temperature and salinity, so it already contains temperature. **It is never an outcome here.** `D` contains temperature through `C_sat` deliberately — that is the *subtraction* of the solubility channel, the equation coming from outside the archive — and errors in temperature enter `D` but not the year regressor, so they add noise, not trend.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-CIRC "What this claim rests on")</sup> See also [C6](../hypodrafts/C6.md "Water temperature and solubility").

## The null, under the constraint actually imposed

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-NULLDESIGN">Not “zero slope”. The estimator is a within-cell fixed-effect slope on year; the constraint imposed is *within station and within calendar month*. The null is a **year-block procedure**: resample the calendar years with replacement, and separately permute year labels attached to whole years, refitting on each draw. That keeps every station effect, the seasonal cycle and the within-year common shock, destroying only the ordering of years against outcome.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-NULLDESIGN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-DEPEND">Whether the dependence the textbook standard error ignores is temporal — a cell's years following one another — or cross-sectional — every cell in a year sampling the same weather — has not been measured here; the year-block null holds under both, and the naive standard error is to be reported beside the block one, with their ratio.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-DEPEND "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Composition, handled

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-NOLABEL">No script in this repository defines a split of the stations by the season they are sampled in, so no such label enters this design.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-NOLABEL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-DEFENCES">If the mix of stations moves, it can tilt a pooled slope; the defences required are (i) within-cell fixed effects, so a station only competes with itself, and (ii) the balanced panel, so entry and exit cannot tilt the slope.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-DEFENCES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Procedure

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-P1">Read `oxy_bed`, `temp_bed`, `sal_bed`, `temp_surf` and `sal_surf` at the offsets the `.json` gives, keyed `station×1000 + month`; apply stated plausibility bounds on value, counting what each removes; compute `C_sat` and `D`; build the trend panel.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-P1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-P2">Fixed-effect slopes on year for `O`, `C_sat`, `D`, `T_bed` and `T_surf − T_bed`. The slopes of `O`, `C_sat` and `D` satisfy the identity exactly; report the split as a **share of `dO/dt`**, not a p-value.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-P2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-P3">Year-block null (above) for each; report the naive standard error, the block standard error and their ratio.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-P3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
4. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-P4">Repeat on the balanced panel, on June–September and on December–March. **Agreement across the variants is the finding; disagreement is equally the finding.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-P4 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
5. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-P5">Refit `dD/dt` with surface-minus-bed density as a covariate — this *uses* [C1](../hypodrafts/C1.md "Stratification strength")'s variable and does not test it. What survives is the metabolic-plus-unknown residue, a residue, not a `Q10`.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-P5 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What a result would and would not license

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-WOULD">**Would.** If `dC_sat/dt` matches or exceeds `dO/dt` under the year-block null and across the variants, that licenses: *at the trend panel's stations the long-term near-bed oxygen decline is accounted for by the solubility ceiling alone, and the non-thermodynamic deficit did not widen.* That constrains [G1](../hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming")'s headline directly: “monotone worsening independent of load” would be true of the water and still not evidence that load reduction failed, the falling term being the one no load policy touches.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-WOULD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-GI-G1-WOULDNOT">**Would not.** It does not measure respiration and cannot: `D` is a standing stock, a respiration rate is a rate, and converting between them needs a ventilation timescale the archive does not hold. A narrowing `D` is equally consistent with load reduction working *and* with the network drifting toward better-ventilated positions — the defences bound that, they do not eliminate it. It says nothing about stratification beyond a difference between the top and the bottom of the sampled range, which is no pycnocline ([C1](../hypodrafts/C1.md "Stratification strength")'s object), nothing about water bodies, nothing about the stations the span filter drops. And `dD/dt ≈ 0` refutes `G1-b` only at the resolution of monthly medians taken at an unrecorded hour.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-WOULDNOT "What this claim rests on")</sup>
